Compute node centralities of an htna network

Source: R/centralities.R
centralities_htna.Rd

centralities_htna() computes the node centralities of an htna network, with the actor type of every code kept. Centrality measures rank the codes of a transition network by their position in it: how much transition probability a code sends and receives (out- and in-strength), how close it is to the other codes (closeness), how often it lies on the shortest paths between other codes (betweenness), and how far its influence spreads (diffusion). Because the actor type is kept, the table shows whether the human or the AI codes hold the central positions, for example which actor's codes broker the hand-overs.

centralities_htna() computes nine measures: OutStrength, InStrength, ClosenessIn, ClosenessOut, Closeness, Betweenness, BetweennessRSP (randomized shortest-path betweenness), Diffusion and Clustering (weighted clustering coefficient). Path-based measures treat a larger transition weight as a shorter distance (the weights are inverted); strength, diffusion and clustering use the weights as they are. For a grouped network the measures are computed per cohort. It returns a data frame with one row per code (per cohort and code for a grouped network) and one column per measure.

Draw the result with plot_centralities(). To check whether the ranking of the codes would survive dropping sessions use centrality_stability_htna().

Usage

centralities_htna(
  x,
  measures = c("OutStrength", "InStrength", "ClosenessIn", "ClosenessOut", "Closeness",
    "Betweenness", "BetweennessRSP", "Diffusion", "Clustering"),
  ...
)

Arguments

x

An htna network from build_htna() or an htna_group.

measures

Names of the measures to compute. Default: all nine.

...

Further arguments for the centrality computations.

Value

A data frame of class c("htna_centralities", "data.frame"), one row per node, with columns node, actor (its actor type) and one numeric column per measure. For an htna_group, the rows of all cohorts are stacked (one row per cohort and node) with a leading group column.

Conditions

htna_bad_input when x is not an htna network or a measure name is unknown; htna_empty_input for a grouped network without cohorts; htna_unnamed_nodes when the nodes of the network have no names.

See also

plot_centralities(), centrality_stability_htna(), edge_betweenness_htna()

Examples

data(human_ai)
net <- build_htna(human_ai, actor_type = "actor_type")
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'session_date' (1 sessions), 'cluster' (42 sessions), 'actor_type' (24 sessions)
centralities_htna(net)
#> Note: Weights inverted (1/w^1) for path-based measures (invert_weights=TRUE). Higher weights = shorter paths.
#> Note: Weights inverted (1/w^1) for path-based measures (invert_weights=TRUE). Higher weights = shorter paths.
